astra.note: The scout gave no number, so there was nothing to check. The paper prints Table 1 on page 17. Its serves value of both overstates the paper for the reason on page 3. The ICML 2025 venue is not printed on the first page.

joint_evidence: Pages 2 and 3: separate models each trained on images of a single object at one location, composed at inference. One variant (Figure 3, setting C) trains on images holding 1 to 5 objects, but the method does not require them.
best_idea: Defines a composition as a distribution that matches each source model on that model's own projected features, and proves that a linear combination of scores reaches it when the sources have factorized conditionals.
best_headline: CLEVR, composing N = 4 single-object location models, 100 hand-counted samples: 98 of 100 images had all 4 objects in the correct locations with an empty background, against 0 of 100 with the unconditional background (77 had no correct object, 23 had one).
read_scope: Abstract, pages 1 to 5 setup and definition, CLEVR passages, page 9 passage on text-to-image, Table 1 on page 17 read from the page image

claude.headline: right
claude.note: Table 2(b), K = 256: analytic 1.4670, N = 10000 2.6706. The claim that correction cannot fix the error is the paper's stated conjecture (page 1).

astra.headline: right
astra.note: Table 1(d) on page 10 prints all four values. Its serves value of both overstates the paper: a text-to-image model (FLUX.1-schnell) only generated the room dataset (page 31) and is never composed.

joint_evidence: Page 1: the task is generating combinations outside the trained conditions, and page 9 also tests experts each trained on one condition. The room experiment does include couch-plus-object images by design: weight 0.49 per condition in the in-distribution setting and a small base weight (beta = 0.05/3) in the out-of-distribution setting (page 11).
best_idea: Separates sampler approximation error from score estimation error and shows that when the composed target lies outside the training support, score error dominates and Feynman-Kac correction makes it worse.
best_headline: Non-factorized out-of-distribution Gaussian, model trained on N = 10000 samples: sliced Wasserstein-2 distance to the target rises from 0.8518 with K = 1 particle to 2.8322 with K = 256, while with analytic scores it falls from 0.6375 to 0.0820.
read_scope: Abstract, introduction pages 1 and 2, setup page 5, experiments pages 9 to 12, Tables 1 and 2 read from page images, expert passage pages 9 and 27, Appendix F.3 pages 31 and 32

astra.headline: right

joint_evidence: Page 4, Algorithm 1 and Eq. 12: the corrector uses the joint prompt C and each single-concept prompt. No extra training (page 1).
best_idea: During early sampling, CO3 boosts the joint prompt's prediction and subtracts the single-concept predictions in Tweedie-denoised space, so the sample moves away from modes dominated by one concept.
best_headline: Attend-and-Excite Animal-Animal prompts, BLIP-VQA: 0.7441 for CO3 against 0.6950 for SDXL and 0.6980 for Attend-and-Excite.

astra.headline: right
astra.note: Table 1 on page 8 prints 0.8311 and 0.5950. Appendix A on page 15 states the exclusion of images lacking all foreground objects. Its serves value of both overstates the paper: the early sampling stage needs a prompt naming all objects (page 4), which problem 1 forbids.

joint_evidence: Page 4: the first sampling stage uses the base model with a multi-object prompt such as 'a cat and a dog playing with a ball'. The concept models are fine-tuned individually.
best_idea: Samples early steps from the base model with a prompt naming all objects, extracts a region mask per object, then blends the individually fine-tuned concept models region by region in Tweedie-denoised space.
best_headline: Multi-concept image generation over ten concept combinations: CLIP image similarity 0.8311 and DINO image similarity 0.5950 for TweedieMix, against 0.8095 and 0.5352 for Concept Weaver, with images lacking a foreground object excluded from scoring.
best_where: Page 8, Table 1; exclusion on page 15, Appendix A
read_scope: Abstract, introduction, method page 4, evaluation settings and Table 1 on page 8 read from the page image, Appendix A on page 15

claude.headline: not found
claude.note: The scout's 'not stated' is accurate: MNIST is assessed qualitatively (page 12) and the Gaussian errors appear only as a plot (Figure 2, page 10). Its direct rival label is too strong: there is no number to compare on, and no sample shows two objects. The two MNIST models also share digit 1 (training digits {1,6} and {1,7}, page 12), so their data is not disjoint.

joint_evidence: Pages 11 and 12: two models are trained separately on digit sets {1,6} and {1,7} and combined at sampling with no joint images or prompt. The sets overlap on digit 1.
best_idea: Generalizes Feynman-Kac correctors with weighted particles so that samples follow an arbitrary function of several pretrained diffusion models' densities, with optional reward steering.
best_headline: No comparable number is printed: MNIST results are assessed qualitatively, and Gaussian KL and L2 error against particle count appear only as a plot.
read_scope: Abstract, introduction, Algorithm 1 on page 8, Gaussian experiment pages 9 and 10, MNIST experiment pages 11 to 14

claude.headline: right
claude.note: Table 2, CMNIST: OR-ME 98.0 against 77.0, AND 80.4 for both. Its serves value of both is not supported: page 8 says the work composes attributes using a single conditional model, and no experiment targets two separate objects. Its needs_joint_data of 'not stated' can be answered as partly.

joint_evidence: Page 8: scores come from a single conditional model trained over attributes. Pages 4 and 5 add a noise-aware classifier or score-based estimate. Colour and digit sit on the same CMNIST image, and a search of the paper finds no held-out combination. No joint prompt is needed.
best_idea: Derives exact guidance for Boolean formulas over attributes by weighting atomic conditional scores with time-dependent posterior probabilities, when the formula's circuit combines conditionally independent or mutually exclusive parts.
best_headline: CMNIST conformity score on mutually exclusive OR: 98.0% for LogDiff against 77.0% for constant guidance; on AND both score 80.4%.
read_scope: Abstract, introduction, guidance passages pages 2 to 5, Table 2 on page 5 read from the page image, related work on page 8, Appendix D pages 19 to 21, Appendix E on page 23

claude.headline: right
claude.note: Table 3, Score rows: HMC-3C 13.3, Reverse 31.8. Its serves value of both overstates the paper: the experiments are a 2D product of two densities and classifier guidance, with no text-to-image model and no two-object image.

joint_evidence: Page 10: a 2D Gaussian mixture and a uniform density are composed by multiplication. Page 12: an unconditional diffusion model plus a time-dependent classifier on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet.
best_idea: Adds a Metropolis-Hastings-like acceptance step to score-based diffusion by estimating energy differences through line integrals of the score, so MCMC correction works without an energy model.
best_headline: CIFAR-100 classifier-full guidance, 50k samples, score model: FID 13.3 with HMC-3C against 31.8 with the reverse process.
read_scope: Abstract, introduction, experiment passages pages 9 to 13, Table 3 on page 13 read from the page image

astra.headline: right
astra.note: Table 1, N = 6: objDetect 35.8 +/- 5.3, attnScore 25.2 +/- 4.7, SDXL 19.2 +/- 3.3. Table 1 covers N = 4, 5 and 6 only. Faster R-CNN is on page 10, YOLOv11-L on page 9, and the co-occurring COCO object sets on page 8.

joint_evidence: Pages 5 and 8: the prompt lists all target objects, and the first stage generates a subset of N - 1 objects jointly. No model training.
best_idea: Generates all but one of the requested objects first, then inpaints the remaining object into free space with layout guidance, choosing which object to hold back from attention maps or a detector.
best_headline: MS COCO object sets, N = 6, success rate over 5 seeds: 35.8 +/- 5.3% for condComp (objDetect) against 19.2 +/- 3.3% for SDXL and 0.0% for Compositional Generation.
read_scope: Abstract, problem setup and method pages 4 to 8, evaluation setup and Table 1 on pages 8 and 9 read from the page image, variants on page 10

astra.headline: right
astra.note: Table 1, GPT-4o column: ToMe 0.9549, SDXL 0.4907, on the authors' own 50-prompt benchmark (page 7). Its direct rival label is too strong: the method targets binding an object to its attributes and sub-objects.

joint_evidence: Page 7: a single prompt naming both objects is parsed with SpaCy, for example 'a [objectA] with a [itemA] and a [objectB] with a [itemB]'. No model training.
best_idea: Merges each object's attribute and sub-object tokens into one composite token so they share a cross-attention map, then refines that token in early steps with an entropy loss and a semantic binding loss.
best_headline: GPT-4o object binding benchmark, 50 two-object prompts: 0.9549 for ToMe against 0.4907 for SDXL.
best_where: Page 8, Table 1; benchmark defined on page 7
read_scope: Abstract, introduction pages 1 to 3, benchmark and implementation on page 7, Table 1 on page 8 read from the page image

best_headline: GenEval agrees with human annotators on 83% of images, against 88% pairwise agreement between annotators and 80% for CLIPScore, over 6,000 annotations on 1,200 images.

astra.note: Table 1 and Section 3.3. The 17.7 is the Without Rewriting column (reported 75.4, human 93.1). With Rewriting the deviation is 14.6.

joint_evidence: Pages 4 and 5: benchmark prompts name up to 3 objects from a template. This is the evaluation prompt only: no generator training on these targets.

claude.headline: right
claude.note: Table 1: F1 (counting) 0.82 against 0.73, accuracy (spatial) 0.36 against 0.19. The ECCV 2024 venue is not printed in the PDF.

joint_evidence: Page 5: generation is conditioned on a prompt holding all subjects plus their bounding boxes. No model training (page 1).
best_idea: Bounds the cross-attention and self-attention of each subject during sampling so features do not leak between subjects, guided by a given bounding-box layout.
best_headline: DrawBench: counting F1 0.82 and spatial accuracy 0.36 for Bounded Attention, against 0.73 and 0.19 for Stable Diffusion.
read_scope: Abstract, introduction, leakage and method passages pages 3 to 5, quantitative results and Table 1 on page 9 read from the page image

astra.headline: right
astra.note: Table 1, ABC-6K, concept separation: SynGen 28.00, A&E 11.17. The values are shares of three-rater majority votes normalized to sum to 100, and 50.17 had no majority winner. Its direct rival label is too strong: the method targets attribute binding, and a vote share among four compared models is not a rate another method could be scored on.

joint_evidence: Pages 1 and 3: the method parses one prompt holding all entities and modifiers with spaCy, then applies its attention loss during inference. No retraining.
best_idea: Parses the prompt into entities and their modifiers, then optimizes the latent during sampling so each entity's attention map overlaps its modifiers and stays apart from other entities.
best_headline: ABC-6K human evaluation, concept separation as share of majority votes: 28.00 for SynGen against 11.17 for Attend-and-Excite, with 50.17 having no majority winner.
read_scope: Abstract, introduction, method passages pages 2 and 3, datasets and human evaluation pages 5 and 6, Table 1 on page 7 read from the page image
